root_cause.text: In `damon_stat_start()`, when `damon_call()` fails, the previously allocated `damon_ctx` object is not deallocated, causing a memory leak on subsequent calls because the pointer is overwritten without freeing the old context.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix potential resource conflict by ensuring damon_stat_start cannot reinitialize while a context is running, and properly cleans up a stale context before reuse.
intent_record.what: In damon_stat_start, before creating a new context via damon_stat_build_ctx(), added a block that checks if damon_stat_context is non-NULL; if it is, checks if damon_is_running(damon_stat_context) returns true, then returns -EAGAIN, otherwise destroys the context with damon_destroy_ctx(damon_stat_context).
intent_record.how: This change prevents starting a new DAMON monitoring session if there is already a running context, returning an error in that case; if a non-running context exists, it cleans it up before creating a new one.

intent_record.intent_summary: After destroying the DAMON context, set the pointer to NULL to prevent use-after-free errors.
intent_record.what: Added assignment of NULL to damon_stat_context after it is destroyed in damon_stat_stop.
intent_record.how: Prevents potential use-after-free by clearing the pointer to the destroyed context, making subsequent accesses safe if checked against NULL.

relevance_review.reason: Group 0 directly addresses the memory leak by ensuring proper cleanup of a stale context before reuse, which is the core issue of the vulnerability.
Group 1 addresses preventing use-after-free by NULLing the pointer after destruction, not the memory leak from failing to deallocate the old context when damon_call() fails.

candidates.rationale: This assignment overwrites the damon_stat_context pointer without freeing the previously allocated context. If damon_call() fails later in the function, the old context remains allocated and is leaked on subsequent calls when this line executes again.
